q: We did the modified Oh Crap method with my older son when he was 3yo but I’m not sure we can apply the same training method with my second babe.
cx: Second child, two, shows readiness; parent unsure the first child's method fits.

q: I don’t want to lose this potential golden moment where he’s gung-ho to be out of his diapers.
cx: Fears missing the window of interest.

q: This is our only child, but she goes to a pre-K program where everyone else is potty trained, including younger kids and that doesn’t seem to motivate her at all.
cx: Four-year-old still not trained after a regression at three.

q: We also tried doing a two week reset where we didn’t talk about the toilet and just let her void in pull-ups to see if it was psychological and if taking some pressure off would help. That didn’t work either.
cx: Backing off tried and failed.

q: NOTHING is working at this point. She’s got a year to go to kindergarten. I’m at the point where the joy of parenting is completely overshadowed by the frustration and disappointment of this lack of success.
cx: Year-long stuck point with kindergarten ahead.

q: I am always a little heartened to see that we’re not alone on this thread, but I feel very alone.
cx: Returning poster a year later.

q: I’m ready for my day to be over and it’s not even noon yet. I’m currently sitting in the bathroom so I don’t lose my mind.
cx: Parent of two toddlers after a morning of crying and fighting.

q: Everyone who has met him has told me that his is the busiest toddler they have seen (not an award I was hoping for)
cx: 19-month-old who bites and hits the parent constantly.

q: I have tried the calm but firm "no biting biting hurts" and it does literally nothing. I have modeled gentil hands. I have tried redirecting.
cx: Standard biting scripts tried.

q: I have bruises all over my arms and legs from bites.
cx: Parent home most days with the toddler.

q: What are some uncommon things you found helped? Anything I can google i have already tried. Trust me.
cx: Asking past the standard advice.

q: Thank you so much for the book recs. I will definelty be getting these!
cx: Plans to buy books commenters suggested.

q: I used the Oh Crap method to potty train my 23 month old at the start of April, by 4 weeks I would say he was pretty much trained and accidents subsided.
cx: Child trained, moved to underwear, then regressed.

q: I have no idea what happened, but was wondering if this is typical? And any guidance for this? I am so confused because I thought we were doing so well, SIGH.
cx: Regression after the move to underwear.

q: I recently became a SAHM and pulled him out of daycare for financial reasons so my husband works and I stay home with our son. Since then he has been very violent when he tries to express himself- hitting me, slamming things into my face (gave me black eye), biting, punching, throwing.
cx: New stay-at-home mother of an almost-two-year-old.

q: Sometimes I can’t even get him to eat for me but if someone else feeds him he eats no problem. I have no support from my family.
cx: Child behaves differently with others.

q: I’m trying to navigate grief as well I just lost a sibling and I haven’t been able to process that.
cx: Her own bereavement alongside the toddler's aggression.

q: I don’t believe in physical punishment but i will speak with a firm tone and he just laughs.
cx: Firm voice gets laughter.

q:
Ok so before you say "just take away the diapers" let me explain my hesitation.

We initially tried the oh-crap 3 day method and removed diapers which led to holding until she was having sobbing meltdowns.
cx: Child turning three who holds for hours.

q: We quit and tried again at 2 and a half.  This time I did a lot more set-up with Miss Rachel and Elmo and books in the week leading up to it.
cx: Second attempt with more preparation.

q: I'm not sure if I should push her potty success and remove her diapers again, trusting that the successful experience will get her to stop holding, or if this would turn it back into a battle of wills and we'd lose the little progress we've gained.  I've lost all confidence in my judgement on this topic. 🥲
cx: First pees on the potty after a year of pauses.

q: I particularly would love to hear from others that have dealt with strong willed champion holders.
cx: Wants advice from parents with this kind of child.

q: If it helps I don't think the oh-crap method is a bad method and we probably did make mistakes but regardless it's not helpful *now.*  I'm not exactly going to do that method at this point with the current issues we have.
cx: Pushback on a commenter correcting her account of the book.

q: I think this is why our little bathtime routine finally broke through regarding pee - consistent and low pressure, like we didn't care at all it was just a thing to do.
cx: What finally worked for pee.

q: I have two older sons and then my 4 year old daughter. My daughter has been a huge learning curve- everything I thought I knew with her brothers, I had to throw out the window with her.
cx: Experienced parent stumped by the third child.

q: She has terrible tantrums but I've chalked it up to her age. She's perfectly behaved at school.
cx: Behaviour only at home.

q: I can't have a 4 year old on top of me at all times, following me around, constantly whining and talking in a baby voice, randomly crying in fear.

q: I always thought that this was a good parenting tactic but maybe it's not good for her.
cx: Rethinking making children wait for requests.
